Preventive notes

  • Include eccentric quadriceps loading (slow step-downs) to condition the tendons for the repeated impact of race walking.
  • Add lateral and frontal plane work (banded side steps, single-leg balance) for hip stability and knee alignment.
  • Re-assess technique on video every four weeks, from the same rear and side positions, so changes are comparable.

8. SPORTS SCIENCE RELATED SUGGESTIONS

Generic guidance. Generic guidance carried over from the analysis prompt template. Not derived from this video. Review with a qualified sports dietitian, physiotherapist or coach.

Monitoring

  • Use a GPS watch or a shoe-mounted accelerometer to check cadence, ground contact time and vertical oscillation against the video-derived values.
  • Compare video cadence with wearable cadence to cross-validate both.
  • Log perceived exertion (RPE 1-10) beside pace to find an individual lactate-threshold walking speed.

Nutrition

WhenAdvice
Pre-session (2-3 h before)Carbohydrate-rich meal, about 2 g of carbohydrate per kg of body mass.
In-session (over 60 min)Electrolytes about every 45 min and 30-60 g of carbohydrate per hour from gel or drink.
Post-session (within 30 min)Carbohydrate to protein about 3:1 or 4:1, for example a banana and a protein shake.

Recovery

  • Active recovery walks below 60 percent of maximum pace on off days, 20-30 min.
  • Sleep 7-9 hours a night; elevate the legs for 10-15 min after heavy sessions.
  • Cold-water immersion at 10-12 C for 10-15 min after race-pace simulations or heavy load weeks, if it suits the athlete.
  • Compression garments for the lower legs after training, to support venous return.

Psychology

  • Break a session into segments, each with one technique cue at the checkpoint.
  • Rehearse race-day conditions at the same time of day as the target event.
  • Build a short cue-word ladder for technical breakdown, for example: hips, straight, swing, relax.

Periodization

BlockDurationFocusVolumeIntensity
General preparation4-6 weeksAerobic base and technique correction+10-20% per weekAll walks below RPE 7.5 (Zone 2)
Specific preparation4-6 weeksRace-pace capacity and strength workBase volume maintained1-2 speed sessions per week
Competition2-4 weeksTaper and peak performance-30% to -50%Sharpening intensity only

9. LIMITATIONS AND CAVEATS

  • Contact (Rule 54.1) and the bent-knee rule (Rule 54.2) are judged by human judges with the naked eye. This report is a pose-based screen that flags moments for review. It is not a ruling and it cannot say whether a warning or disqualification would follow.
  • Pose estimation from one camera measures depth poorly. Knee and hip flexion are depth-derived from a rear or front view, so results from those views carry a lower confidence ceiling than results from a side view.
  • Risk levels are provisional screening heuristics defined in config/risk_rules.yaml. They are not validated clinical thresholds and this report does not diagnose any condition.
  • No reference values are used unless they carry a citation in config/benchmarks.json. Where none exists the report says so.
  • Sections 7 and 8 contain generic guidance carried over from the analysis template. It was not derived from this video and should be reviewed by a qualified coach, sports dietitian or physiotherapist.
